screen16-a1.glyph: gold crown with a red jewel
screen16-a1.description: gold crown picture in the top bar, left of the gear
screen16-a1.location: top right, first of two pictures
screen16-a1.accessibility_text_consulted: resource_id iv_premium told me to watch for a premium/subscription page; no content_desc or talkback label exists; not used in the verdict
screen16-a1.convention_relied_on: a crown is used by some freemium apps to mark a paid tier, but it is not an established convention a first-time user of mobile apps would read as an action — my reading, confidence medium
screen16-a1.initial_rationale: no word anywhere near it, and a crown is decoration or a brand mark to a first-time user rather than a known control glyph
screen16-a1.deciding_evidence: no visible label in any state; the crown opened a paid subscription offer, which nothing on the screen announced — tested once on screen1-a1; this is a duplicate of that control and the verdict is carried here
screen16-a1.recommendation: add a visible caption such as "Premium" (or "Go Premium") under or beside the crown

screen16-a2.glyph: gear with a wrench laid across it
screen16-a2.description: gear with a wrench laid across it, top bar far right
screen16-a2.accessibility_text_consulted: resource_id iv_setting told me to watch for a Settings page; no content_desc or talkback label; not used in the verdict
screen16-a2.convention_relied_on: gear = settings, an established mobile convention (the wrench overlay does not change the reading) — my reading, confidence high
screen16-a2.initial_rationale: unlabeled, but a gear is a widely known settings convention — common-icon exemption pending the behavioural test
screen16-a2.deciding_evidence: the gear opened the Settings page, exactly as the gear convention promises — tested once on screen1-a2; this is a duplicate of that control and the verdict is carried here

screen16-a3.description: pill-shaped chip reading "PDF" in the file-type row under the title (drawn as the current/selected item; tapping the current item changes nothing but the item carries the selected state, so it stays in scope)
screen16-a3.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "PDF" repeats the visible word; not used in the verdict
screen16-a3.initial_rationale: "PDF" is a widely known document type; in a row of file types on a document reader the chip reads as "show PDF files", and the filled chip shows which is current
screen16-a3.deciding_evidence: the tap switched the selected file type to PDF, as the word on it predicts — tested once on screen1-a3; this is a duplicate of that control and the verdict is carried here

screen16-a4.description: pill-shaped chip reading "HWP" in the file-type row under the title
screen16-a4.location: top, second chip in the row
screen16-a4.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "HWP" repeats the visible word; not used in the verdict
screen16-a4.initial_rationale: "HWP" is a file-format abbreviation (a Korean word-processor format) that a first-time user outside that market will not recognise; next to PDF/Word/Excel/PPT it reads as a file type, but nothing says which files or what pressing it changes
screen16-a4.deciding_evidence: pressing it only recoloured the chip; neither the chip nor the result ever says what "HWP" is — tested once on screen1-a4; this is a duplicate of that control and the verdict is carried here
screen16-a4.recommendation: spell out the format, e.g. "Hangul (HWP)" or "HWP documents", or drop the chip in locales where the format is not used
